questions.question: Under SEBI regulations, what minimum percentage of Net Distributable Cash Flows (NDCF) must a REIT distribute to unitholders?
questions.explanation: SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 mandate that at least 90% of NDCF must be distributed to unitholders periodically.

questions.question: What is the typical minimum lot size for trading listed REIT units on Indian stock exchanges today?
questions.explanation: SEBI revised trading lot sizes in July 2021 to 1 unit to facilitate easy retail investor participation.

questions.question: What is the primary source of cash distributions paid by commercial office REITs in India?
options: Contractual tenant rentals and corporate lease income
Trading profits from flipping residential apartments
questions.explanation: REITs primarily hold operational commercial offices leased to corporations that pay periodic rental income.

questions.question: How are Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed REIT units taxed if held for more than 12 months (post Finance Act 2024)?
options: 12.5% on cumulative gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh per financial year
At personal marginal income slab rate
questions.explanation: Finance Act 2024 standardized listed equity/REIT LTCG at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh for holding periods exceeding 12 months.

questions.question: What happens to the distribution payouts of a REIT if major tenants vacate and buildings have high vacancies?
options: The government guarantees paying the difference to investors
Rental revenue drops, which reduces the Net Distributable Cash Flow payouts
REIT unitholders are personally liable to pay the tenant debt
questions.explanation: Because REIT distributions depend on collected rent, higher vacancies reduce cash available for distribution.
